title: Cc No. 251/2020 Page No.1 /10 Surender ... vs Ekta Bobal on 22 August, 2022
full_text: Cc No. 251/2020 Page No.1 /10 Surender ... vs Ekta Bobal on 22 August, 2022 IN THE COURT OF SH. ABHITESH KUMAR, LD. MM (NI ACT), DIGITAL COURT-04, SOUTH, SAKET COURTS, DELHI. DLST020154492020 SURENDER RANDHAWA S/o Sh. Trilok Singh R/o H.No. 78D, Pushp Vihar, Sec-IV New Delhi - 110017 .... Complainant VERSUS EKTA BOBAL W/o Sh. Raj Kumar Bobal R/o 1/18, Gali No. 1, House No. 18 Ground Floor, DDA Flats, Madangir New Delhi-110062 .... Accused Complainant Case no. 251/2020 CNR No. DLST02-015449-2020 Title SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL Name of Complainant Surender Randhawa Name of accused Ekta Bobal Date of institution of complaint 15.12.2020 Date of arguments 28.07.2022 Date of pronouncement 22.08.2022 Offence complained of Under Section 138 NI Act Offence charged with Under Section 138 NI Act Plea of the accused Pleaded not guilty Final order Acquittal CC No. 251/2020 Page No.1 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL JUDGMENT BRIEF REASONS FOR THE DECISION OF THE CASE:- That present complaint has been filed by the complainant against the accused under section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred as the "Act"). 1. Brief facts of this case is that the complainant and accused are known to each other since last many years and have friendly relation with each other. In the second week of June 2019, the accused approached and requested to the complainant by showing the financial need for urgent requirement of sum of Rs. 100,000/- for his personal work and assured to the complainant for returned the same loan amount within 10 months. 2. That seeing friendly relations, the complainant arranged the said loan amount and handed over a sum of Rs. 100,000/- in cash to the accused on 19.06.2019 and the accused assured the complainant to return the said loan amount within a period of 10 months and executed an agreement and receipt in favour of the complainant. 3. That in order to discharge said liability, accused has issued a cheque bearing no. 543975 dated 24.09.2020 for a sum of Rs. 100,000/- (Ex CW1/3). On presentation, said cheque was returned unpaid with the remark "Funds Insufficient" vide its returning memo dated 08.10.2020 (Ex CW1/4). 4. That the complainant sent a statutory demand notice (Ex CW1/5) on 21.10.2020 through his counsel by Speed Post (Ex CW1/6) on the last known address of the accused. The legal notice was received by the accused (Ex CW1/7) and the accused has send CC No. 251/2020 Page No.2 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL the reply of the said statutory demand notice. When even the demand notice could not give any fruitful results, complainant has filed the instant complaint (Ex CW1/9). 5. Chronology of events are as follows: Date Events Documents 24.09.2020 Cheque Drawn Ex. CW 1/3 08.10.2020 Return Memo Ex. CW 1/4 21.10.2020 Demand Notice Sent Ex. CW1/6 24.10.2020 Demand Notice Ex. CW1/7 Delivered 15.12.2020 Complaint Filed Ex. CW 1/9 6. On finding prima facie case against the accused, the accused Ekta Bobal was summoned to face trial on 11.01.2021. 7. After the appearance of accused, notice u/s 251 CrPC was framed on 05.03.2021. In reply, the accused Ekta Bobal pleaded not guilty and stated in defence that "loan amount taken was Rs. 70,000/- and amount mentioned in the loan agreement is Rs. 100,000 which is not correct and same in the cheques. I have filed a complaint in Police for shuting down my boutique and harrasing me due to which I went into depression." Accused has admitted her signature on cheque in question and also admitted receipt of statutory demand notice. The matter was then put up for Trial (Summary). In terms of Section 294 CrPC, accused has admitted all documents filed by the complainant. 8. On prayer of the accused, this court has permitted her to cross examine the complainant vide order dated 17.02.2022. CE is closed on 08.03.2022. CC No. 251/2020 Page No.3 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL 9. Thereafter, the statement of accused was recorded u/s 313 r/w 281 of CrPC on 04.04.2022 wherein the accused has stated that "I have already made the payments. Complainant has mentally harassed me and forced me to stop my work. I have also made a complaint in Women Cell and PS Ambedkar Nagar against the complainant. Complainant has also harassed my children. I had given 4 blank security cheque for the said loan. After making all the payments I had requested him to return the said blank cheques. He had not returned the said blank cheques and informed me that those cheques have been lost. Complainant has misused those cheques. The cheque in question was one of the blank security cheque.". The accused stated that she intends to lead defence evidence. 10. In DE, DW1 Sushma Soni was examined. DE was closed on 27.04.2022. 11. Both the counsels have argued orally. Ld. Counsel for the complainant has reiterated the complaint and also pointed out the contradictions in the version of accused. Ld. LAC for the accused has submitted that large sum of money has already been paid to the complainant and accused does not have liability to pay Rs. 1,00,000 i.e. cheque amount. 12. Arguments heard. Documents perused. 13. The law as it stands now is that once the issuance of the cheque is admitted or proved, the trial Court is duty bound to raise the presumption that the dishonoured cheque placed before it was indeed issued in discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability of the amount mentioned therein. That being said let us also point out that the presumption is a rebuttable one. It is up to the accused CC No. 251/2020 Page No.4 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL to prove that the cheque in question had not been issued in discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability. To rebut the presumption accused may dispute the case of complainant or choose to lead evidence. Now the question arises what will be the standard of proof. In Rangappa V. Sri Mohan reported as (2010) 11 SCC 441, Hon'ble SC observed that.... " Section 139 of the Act is an example of a reverse onus clause that has been included in furtherance of the legislative objective of improving the credibility of negotiable instruments. While Section 138 of the Act specifies a strong criminal remedy in relation to the dishonour of cheques, the rebuttable presumption under Section 139 is a device to prevent undue delay in the course of litigation. However, it must be remembered that the offence made punishable by Section 138 can be better described as a regulatory offence since the bouncing of a cheque is largely in the nature of a civil wrong whose impact is usually confined to the private parties involved in commercial transactions. In such a scenario, the test of proportionality should guide the construction and interpretation of reverse onus clauses and the accused/defendant cannot be expected to discharge an unduly high standard of proof. In the absence of compelling CC No. 251/2020 Page No.5 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL justifications, reverse onus clauses usually impose an evidentiary burden and not a persuasive burden. Keeping this in view, it is a settled position that when an accused has to rebut the presumption under Section 139 , the standard of proof for doing so is that of `preponderance of probabilities'. Therefore, if the accused is able to raise a probable defence which creates doubts about the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability, the prosecution can fail. As clarified in the citations, the accused can rely on the materials submitted by the complainant in order to raise such a defence and it is conceivable that in some cases the accused may not need to adduce evidence of his/her own." 14. Therefore, the law as it stands today is that presumption u/s 118(a) r/w 139 of the Act is rebuttable and the standard of proof for accused shall be preponderance of probabilities. 15. In the instant case it is to be noted that accused has admitted all documents filed by the complainant and disputed his complaint only on the point of extent of liability. 16. Complainant case is that he has given Rs. 1,00,000 to the accused and in order to return the said amount accused has issued the cheque in question. Loan agreement and receipt is proved as Ex. CW1/1 and Ex. CW1/2 respectively. But during cross examination complainant has said that he had given Rs. 2,00,000 to the accused CC No. 251/2020 Page No.6 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL in the presence of husband of accused and Ms. Harsha Sivanand. This fact is nowhere mentioned in the complaint or statutory demand notice or Pre-summoning evidence. Complainant's version is contradictory on this point. Complainant has not called Ms. Harsha Sivananda as his witness, reasons best known to him. Now the issue before this court, which statement/version should be believed. To answer, relevant provisions from Indian Evidence Act may be referred. In view of S.91 and 92 of Indian Evidence Act, when any matter is reduced to the form of a document, no oral agreement or statement shall be admitted between the parties for the purpose of contradicting, varying, adding to or subtracting from its terms. In the instant case the Ex. CW1/1 and Ex. CW1/2 shows there was an agreement for Rs. 1,00,000 and accused has received Rs. 1,00,000 only. Loan agreement (Ex. CW1/1) is silent on rate of interest. Therefore, oral testimony for Rs. 2,00,000 cannot be admitted in the absence of any subsequent document or evidence. Accordingly, it is proved that complainant has given Rs. 1,00,000 to the accused and accused has admitted to return the same within the period of 10 months with interest at the rate of 2% per month. On rate of interest suggestion was on behalf of accused and complainant has admitted it during his cross examination. 17. In defence, Mrs. Sushma Soni (DW1) was examined. DW1 is friend of accused and also acquainted with the complainant. DW1 stated that complainant gives money on interest. DW1 has further stated that complainant has given Rs. 80,000 only, after deducting Rs. 10,000 as file charge and Rs. 10,000 as advance, to the accused and accused has already returned the said amount to the CC No. 251/2020 Page No.7 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL complainant. Accused has given 4 security cheque to the complainant. Accused has also filed complaint against the complainant. During cross, DW1 stated that complainant has given Rs. 80,000 to the accused in the month of June 2019 in her presence and one another lady Ms. Deepa was also present there. DW1 has accompanied the accused when accused went to return the money advanced by the complainant. DW1 has also told address of the complainant where she went with the accused to return the aforesaid money. DW1 has further stated that accused has given blank signed cheques to the complainant in her presence. Cheque in question is one of those blank but signed cheque. Accused has requested for receipt of money paid but complainant has not given any receipt. Complainant has visited shop of the accused and abused her. Accused has filed complaint against the complainant. All these aforesaid facts are neither denied nor specifically disputed by the complainant. Only two generic and vague suggestions are raised by the complainant on false deposition and non-issuance of receipt. However, DW1 doesn't remember the amount which was given to complainant on her first visit with the accused but her visit and meeting with the complainant is not disputed. Complainant has also not disputed his acquaintance with DW1. DW1 has said that accused has already repaid the money advanced by the complainant. On close scrutiny of testimony of DW1, this court is of the view that there is nothing on record which discredit her testimony. 18. In reply to statutory demand notice Ex. CW1/8 , accused has expressly admitted that she has not repaid whole money but already paid large sum of money i.e Rs. 84,000 in seven installments till CC No. 251/2020 Page No.8 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL Dec. 2019. The repayment in installments is further corroborated by DW1 when she stated that she had accompanied the accused 3-4 times for repayment of the money and thereafter accused went for repayment with her husband. When whole loan was for Rs. 1,00,000 and large or any amount is paid then it can be categorically understood that accused has no liability to pay Rs.1,00,000 on the date of presentation of cheque. Section 138 of the Act reads that where any cheque was drawn for payment of any amount of money for the discharge in whole or any part of any debt or other liability and the same is dishonoured by the Bank, the person who drew the cheque shall be punished. Therefore, the cheque drawn should be towards the discharge of either the whole debt or part of the debt. If the cheque is more than the amount of the debt due, Section 138 of the Act cannot be attracted. In the instant case total money advanced by the complainant was Rs. 1,00,000 and large part of money has already been repaid by the accused. Contradiction is there among defense raised during framing of notice under section 251 CrPC, statement of accused and testimony of DW1 but those contradictions are minor considering merits of the case and could be overlooked. Contradiction is on the point of amount of repayment but they are consistent on two point firstly that large sum of money is already repaid to the complainant and secondly on the extent of liability. 19. Therefore, in view of above discussion, this court of the considered view that the accused has successfully rebutted the statutory presumption u/s. 118 (a) read with 139 of the Act existed in favour of the complainant by creating reasonable doubt on the CC No. 251/2020 Page No.9 /10 SURENDER RANDHAWA Vs EKTA BOBAL complainant's claim. As settled, if the presumption is rebutted then the burden of proof shifts back to the complainant to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubt. The complainant, in the present case, has neither examined any witness (other than himself) nor filed any document on record to prove the culpability. 20. On evaluation of the entire evidence, this court finds the version of the complainant improbable and difficult to believe. Accused has successfully created doubts on the existence of legal liability of the accused towards the complainant on the date of issuance/drawal of cheque in question. The complainant, thereafter, has not been able to establish that there was a legal debt or liability to the extent of Rs. 1,00,000 was standing on the part of the accused towards the complainant on the date of issuance of cheque. Thus, the most important ingredient of section 138 of the Act has not been fulfilled. 21. In view of above discussion, the accused Ekta Bobal is acquitted for the offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act. Announced in the open Court on 22.08.2022 ABHITESH KUMAR Digital Court-04, South, Saket This Judgment contains ten pages (10) and all pages bears my digital signature.
